strings.about.title: About Git Messages
strings.about.body: Git Messages is a curated reference for commit message conventions and a tool for composing clear messages.
strings.about.detail: It covers Conventional Commits and Angular-style messages, including types, emoji mappings, examples, and reusable templates.

strings.privacy.title: Privacy
strings.privacy.body: This service serves a static, curated commit convention catalog. It does not provide user accounts, accept user submissions, or persist personal data. Operational logs may be handled by the server operator.

strings.terms.body: The catalog is provided as a reference. Check the selected convention and your repository's contribution rules before using a generated message.

strings.mcp.title: Git Messages MCP connection help
strings.mcp.help.description: Connect to the public catalog and stateless message builder using Streamable HTTP.
strings.mcp.help.auth: Use a linked Bearer token in the Authorization header. Create one for this MCP client on the API tokens page; every MCP request requires it.
strings.mcp.help.overview: Use Git Messages as an MCP server to browse its curated commit conventions or build a message.
strings.mcp.help.endpoint: POST /api/v1/server/mcp is the canonical Streamable HTTP endpoint. /api/mcp and /mcp are direct aliases.
strings.mcp.help.authentication: MCP uses the same Bearer tokens as the REST API. Create a linked token for this client on the API tokens page; there is no separate MCP token.
strings.mcp.help.connect: Send JSON-RPC 2.0 with Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream, and the negotiated MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, and tool-call Mcp-Name headers.
strings.mcp.help.limits: Requests are limited to 1 MiB and use the same public API rate limits. Calls do not store data.
strings.mcp.help.troubleshooting: Check that the protocol version in params._meta matches MCP-Protocol-Version and that any Origin is the request origin or an explicitly configured origin.
strings.mcp.help.project: This server exposes only the public catalog and stateless builder. It has no user-owned resources or token-management tools.
strings.mcp.help.status_200: Request accepted; inspect the JSON-RPC result for tool errors.
strings.mcp.help.status_400: Invalid JSON-RPC body, protocol version, or required MCP header.
strings.mcp.help.status_401: Bearer token is missing or invalid.
strings.mcp.help.status_headers: Use POST with the required Content-Type and Accept headers.

strings.help.getting_started_body: Browse commit types and conventions, choose a template, or open the message builder to create a message.
strings.help.using_catalog_body: Use the type and convention references to check meaning and format. Templates provide starting points; random endpoints return examples. The browser builder validates a type, scope and description, then displays the resulting commit message.
strings.help.account_question: Do I need an account or token?
strings.help.account_answer: No account is required for the public catalog or message builder.
strings.help.submission_question: Can I submit commit messages or conventions?
strings.help.submission_answer: No. The catalog is curated and read-only, and builder requests are stateless.
strings.help.troubleshooting_body: If a message cannot be built, check that its type is listed and its description is a single line. API clients should check the response status and error body for invalid input.

strings.privacy.collection_body: The catalog is embedded in the application and is not submitted by visitors. The service processes request metadata for operation and abuse prevention. Contact and security reports contain the information the sender provides.
strings.privacy.usage_body: Data is used to provide the service, protect it from abuse, and respond to reports. It is not used for targeted advertising.
strings.privacy.security_body: The service applies access controls and security protections to operational state and report data. Operators should use HTTPS, protect configuration and key material, and keep the server software current.
strings.privacy.retention.period: Resources you create are kept until they expire or you delete them with your owner token. Preferences are stored only in cookies in your browser. Operational logs are kept for up to 30 days. Anonymized analytics data may be retained for up to 12 months.

strings.security.policy.default:
## Scope
The application served at {host}, including its API.

## Out of scope
Denial of service and volumetric testing, social engineering of operators or users, physical attacks, findings in third-party services or dependencies without an exploitable path here, automated scanner output without demonstrated impact, and missing best-practice headers on non-sensitive pages.

## Coordinated disclosure
Please report privately through /server/security and allow 90 days from the report to publish. The window ends early once a fix is released and may be extended by agreement.

## Safe harbor
Good-faith research that follows this policy, avoids privacy violations and service disruption, accesses only what is needed to show the issue, and stops when it has done so is authorized. No legal action will be taken for it.

## Reporting
Use /server/security.

strings.overlay.tor.title: Tor Access
strings.overlay.tor.description: This application is available as a Tor hidden service for enhanced privacy.
strings.overlay.tor.step.connect: Open Tor Browser and wait for it to connect.
strings.overlay.tor.step.open: Copy the onion address above and paste it into the Tor Browser address bar.
strings.overlay.tor.note: Using Tor provides additional privacy by hiding your IP address and routing your connection through the Tor network.
strings.overlay.i2p.title: I2P Access
strings.overlay.i2p.description: This application is available as an I2P eepsite for enhanced privacy.
strings.overlay.i2p.step.proxy: Configure your browser to use the I2P HTTP proxy (default 127.0.0.1:4444).
strings.overlay.i2p.step.open: Copy the .b32.i2p address above and paste it into your browser address bar.
strings.overlay.i2p.note: I2P routes your connection through the I2P network. Eepsites use http://; the I2P tunnel provides transport encryption, so no TLS certificate is used.
